review_notes: Read the whole file and grepped for uses of the caratheodory lemmas. The simp set is mostly reasonable. isCaratheodory_empty and isCaratheodory_compl_iff are simp, and the local simp commutativity lemmas are permutation lemmas, so I found no loop risk. The one inconsistency I found is top_caratheodory, which is the only one of the zero/top/dirac "= ⊤" caratheodory lemmas without @[simp]. I did not run Lean. Whether simp would then close the side goal at the one use site depends on how the goal is presented, so I did not check that.

findings.problem: The sibling lemmas `zero_caratheodory` and `dirac_caratheodory` have the same shape (`_.caratheodory = ⊤`) and are `@[simp]`. `top_caratheodory` is not. The simp normal form is therefore inconsistent. Simp can simplify the Carathéodory σ-algebra of `0` and of `dirac a`, but not of `⊤`. Its only use, in `toMeasure_top`, rewrites it by hand with `rw [OuterMeasure.top_caratheodory]; exact le_top`. The lemma has no hypotheses and its right-hand side is a simpler term, so tagging it is safe and cannot loop.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `top_caratheodory`, as for `zero_caratheodory` and `dirac_caratheodory`. The `rw ...; exact le_top` side goal in `toMeasure_top` could then become a `simp` call. I did not check that.
findings.benefit: The three canonical `caratheodory = ⊤` facts are then all simp lemmas, so goals that mention `(⊤ : OuterMeasure α).caratheodory` normalize to `⊤` automatically. Users no longer need to find and rewrite with the lemma by name.
